PC: Ask for intravenous (IV) access, to have patient placed on monitor, call for nasal cannula
Promptly perform focused History and Physical Exam
Discover complaints of nausea, abdominal cramping, tearing of his eyes, excessive salivation, sweating profusely and shortness of breath in a farmer
Decontaminate patient by removing clothes and washing patient to remove remaining toxin
Order atropine and pralidoxime as definitive treatment of organophosphate poisoning.Doses utilized at Patan hospital are 1-3 mg atropine IV push doses and 1g of pralidoxime over 1 hour
Continue push doses of atropine until patient clinically improves, which means improvement in vitals as well as decrease in hypersalivation
Recognize patient will need an atropine drip ordered once stabilized with bolus dosing
MK: If learner orders EKG, recognize cause of sinus bradycardia as cholinergic poisoning
Recognize that to obtain proper treatment, high doses of atropine will be needed
SBP: Recognize potential organophosphate poisoning and immediately ensure team safety
Give reusable fabric gowns, gloves, masks to all healthcare workers involved in patient’s care
Call intensive care unit and describe case succinctly
ICS: The learner will take lead and assign clear roles
